findings.description: On SIGINT, the handler releases the lock and kills gate-lock straight away, even though the locked command is still running. `scripts/gate-lock.sh` kept the lock until the command finished.

`LINT_CMD` now gets every changed source file in a single `sh -c` call. `verify.sh` split them into batches through `xargs -0`. Past the kernel's argument-size limit the spawn fails with E2BIG, lint is reported red, and verify can never stamp the tree.
findings.body:
**The lint file list is no longer batched, so a large change set fails to exec (E2BIG)**

`scripts/verify.sh` piped the list through `xargs -0 sh -c "$LINT_CMD \"\$@\"" _`, which splits it into runs that fit under ARG_MAX. The port passes every file in one `execve`:

```rust
spawn_captured(
    Command::new("sh")
        .arg("-c")
        .arg(format!("{lint_cmd} \"$@\""))
        .arg("_")
        .args(&sources),
)
```

The size of `sources` has no bound. When `refs/remotes/origin/<trunk>` does not resolve (the trunk was never fetched, the remote has another name, or `GIT_TRUNK` is wrong), base falls back to the empty tree (L36-44). Every tracked source file then counts as changed. A branch that sweeps a whole monorepo has the same effect.

At roughly 30k paths (2 MiB of arguments plus environment by default), `spawn()` returns `Err(E2BIG)`. The `Some(Err(err))` arm (L99-102) then marks lint red. Re-running changes nothing, so the tree is never stamped and `pre-push` refuses every push.

`quality_checks.rs` already has an `xargs()` batcher (5000 arguments or 128 KiB per run). To keep lint running in the background next to check-agent-config, either run the batches in sequence inside one spawned `sh`, or move the batching loop onto a thread. `pre_commit.rs` L49-54 has the same pattern; it came in with an earlier PR.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c2e7339eceebdfeb5e8b17cf81641be75bbb9ad8/tools/hooks-rs/src/verify.rs#L71-L79

findings.description: `pub fn git_or_exit(args: &[&str]) -> String` copies `crate::added_lines::git_loud(args).unwrap_or_else(|code| exit(code))` line for line. Both inherit stderr, exit 127 when git cannot spawn, exit with git's code (or 1) when it fails, and trim the trailing `\n`. `pre_commit.rs:9`, `worktree_create.rs:25` and `worktree_remove.rs:214` already use the `git_loud` form. Delete the helper and use `git_loud` at all 8 call sites. Delta about -14 +2 (the import swap, and rustfmt may wrap some calls). Behavior holds: same exit codes, same stderr, same trimmed stdout.

Test adequacy: the acquire writes the label before the pid, and no Rust test pins that order. The shell harness did, with `check 'the acquire writes the label before the pid' grep -qF 'mkdir "$LOCK" && echo "$label" >"$LOCK/label" && echo $$ >"$LOCK/pid"' gate-lock.sh`. The Rust port dropped the case, so the "every shell case has a Rust test" claim does not hold here.

Test adequacy: no test checks which files verify hands to the lint command. The fixture `STUB` logs only `$1` (`echo "$1" >>"$STUB_CALLS"`), and `LINT_CMD="stub lint"` ignores the file arguments. Lint is only asserted to run or not run.

The hand-rolled `Command::new("git").args(["rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"]).stderr(Stdio::inherit()).output()...unwrap_or_default()` block equals `git_loud(&["rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"]).unwrap_or_default()`, as `worktree_remove.rs` already does. Delta -10 +2, with the same behavior on failure.

The test `Repo` rebuilds helpers that tests/common already has. Use `common::executable` for the stub write and chmod, `common::path_with` for the PATH built by hand, and `common::git_stdout` for the six-line `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` call. About -14 +3.
The `Repo::commit` body (write the files, `git add -A`, `git commit -qm next`) is duplicated in tests/verify.rs L43-53. It could become a shared `common::commit(dir, files)` helper. About -10 +7.

The shell case 'the pre-commit lints its staged files without waiting for a held lock' (tests/scripts/gate-lock.test.sh L384-390) has no Rust counterpart. A pre-commit that started taking the gate lock would pass every test.

After `create_dir` succeeds, the label and pid files are written with `fs::write`, which follows a symlink. A sandboxed process that shares the lock in `.git` could plant `label` or `pid` as a symlink, and the unsandboxed holder would then overwrite that symlink's target outside the sandbox. The shell original has the same race. Opening both files with `create_new(true)` (O_EXCL) closes it.

`clean()` fails open: when `git status` exits non-zero, `unwrap_or_default()` returns empty output, so the tree counts as clean at both checks. The shell original behaves the same. Treating a git failure as dirty would close it.

pre-commit hands every staged source file to one `sh -c` exec, where `scripts/pre-commit` used `xargs -0`. A very large staged set can fail with E2BIG. This has the same root cause as the verify.rs lint finding, but this code came in with an earlier PR.
